name: Nazmus Shakib Sayom
title: Graduate Research Assistant
bio: Nazmus Shakib Sayom is a PhD student and graduate research assistant in the Kahlert School of Computing at the University of Utah. His work focuses on cyber-physical systems safety and security, with emphasis on system verification, safety falsification, property-guided reduction, and surrogate execution for robotic and autonomous systems.

education.focus: Cyber-physical systems security, falsification, and safety verification for autonomous systems
Summa Cum Laude; CGPA 3.96/4.00; thesis on disaster victim tracking and rescue support systems

experience.summary: Built embedded Linux distributions for ARM platforms with Yocto, OTA update flows, device-service integrations, and security hardening for deployed edge systems.
Taught operating systems, embedded systems, and computer fundamentals while continuing research collaborations and student mentoring.
Led platform work for a jobs marketplace and built IVR-based access paths for users without reliable internet connectivity.
Prototyped IoT and computer-vision systems for self-checkout and centralized advertising delivery.

research_statement: I study how cyber-physical and autonomous systems can be reduced, tested, and checked against safety properties without losing the behaviors that matter.
research_questions: How can complex CPS control stacks be reduced into property-relevant surrogates for scalable falsification?
How can temporal-logic oracles and execution traces expose safety violations in robotic vehicles?
How can embedded and IoT systems be engineered with stronger security and privacy guarantees from sensing through deployment?
